title: How Soap Destroys Germs in Seconds! 🧼
description: Soap doesn't just wash away dirt; it completely destroys germs by tearing apart their fatty membranes. Discover the precise chemical battle between soap and viruses in one minute.

scenes.say: Why is water alone helpless against germs, while soap destroys them in mere seconds?

scenes.caption: Dual action molecule
scenes.say: The secret lies in the soap molecule. It has a water-loving head and a fat-loving tail!
Most viruses and bacteria are protected by a fatty shield. Water just slides right past it, but soap attacks it head-on.
The soap tail plunges into the fatty shield and rips it apart. The germ collapses, and the water washes it all away.

scenes.label: Time needed to clean hands
scenes.say: Soap molecules need at least twenty seconds to completely tear apart virus shells, so never rush your handwashing!
